methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective cohort nested in WHI with baseline and repeated (year 3, 6) DXA body composition data, 27-year follow-up, and adjudicated breast cancer incidence and cause-specific mortality (n=9767 with 738 incident cases, 87 BC deaths). Strengths: Fine-Gray competing risk regression with three nested models to address body-size confounding (height, BMI, SMI), time-varying models using repeated DXA, multiple imputation (MICE) for missing covariates, a priori stratification by age and BMI, pre-specified secondary analyses near diagnosis. Limitations: small event count (87 deaths) limits stratified power, SDOH incompletely captured, baseline DXA may precede diagnosis by decades, pre-diagnosis subgroup (n=297, 24 deaths) severely underpowered. Authors transparently address all these issues.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual prospective cohort maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The findings are clinically relevant for prevention and survivorship: higher VAT, SAT, and TAT are associated with elevated BC mortality (SHR ~1.49, 1.40, 1.26 per 100 cm2), suggesting abdominal adiposity contributes to BC death beyond BMI. The null finding for VAT/SAT ratio and similar magnitudes for VAT vs SAT argue that total abdominal adiposity - not depot distribution - matters for mortality, with practical implications for risk stratification and public-health messaging. Translational path is plausible since DXA is more accessible than CT/MRI.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is appropriate for this observational cohort. Reporting is thorough: clear study population with inclusion/exclusion flow, exposure operationalization (DXA QDR software + APEX 4.0 with validated MRI-based cross-calibration), outcomes adjudicated via standard WHI procedures, covariates defined a priori with justification, statistical methods (Fine-Gray competing risks, MICE imputation, PH assumption testing, VIF collinearity checks), and strengths/limitations discussed extensively. Data availability is limited (WHI data access is request-based) and no code is shared in this paper.

novelty_literature.justification: Prior WHI work on DXA-derived VAT/SAT and BC incidence has been published by the same group (Bea 2025 cited), and CT-based body composition at BC diagnosis (B-SCANS) is well established. The novel contribution is applying DXA-derived VAT/SAT to BC mortality in the prevention setting with long follow-up - a specifically identified gap in the literature. Surprise finding that VAT/SAT ratio is null and SAT matches VAT magnitude is interesting and contrasts with the a priori hypothesis. Extension rather than paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is well-structured, clearly written, and presents complex analyses with appropriate clarity. Abstract includes both a plain-language summary and a structured scientific abstract. Tables and figures are referenced throughout. Discussion is balanced, connects findings to mechanism (hormonal, inflammatory, adipose tissue biology), and integrates prior literature well. Limitations section is unusually thorough and candid. Minor issue: REDACTED placeholder in methods section 2.1 where date range was removed is a normal blinding artifact.

key_strengths: Large prospective WHI cohort with 27-year adjudicated follow-up, repeated DXA scans, and Fine-Gray competing risk regression
APEX 4.0 DXA-derived VAT/SAT previously validated against MRI in the same cohort
Rigorous handling of body-size confounding via nested models (height, BMI, SMI) with VIF reporting and explicit acknowledgement of collinearity
Time-varying analyses and pre-diagnosis sensitivity analysis address reverse causation concerns
Transparent, thorough limitations section acknowledging power, SDOH, and temporal gap between baseline DXA and mortality
key_concerns: Only 87 BC deaths limit statistical power, especially for stratified and interaction analyses
Pre-diagnosis secondary analysis (n=297, 24 deaths) is underpowered and null; authors appropriately note this
Baseline DXA may be up to two decades before diagnosis in some participants, limiting biological inference about adiposity immediately preceding cancer
No code release and limited external replication potential given WHI-specific cohort
Surprise finding that SAT ~ VAT contradicts prior CT-based literature and a priori hypothesis; mechanistic interpretation remains speculative
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically rigorous observational cohort using validated DXA measures with long follow-up; contributes a prevention-setting perspective on abdominal adiposity and BC mortality. Fits Tier 3 with minor revisions.
